report: Andrea was visited by her daughter this afternoon. Despite her daughter's encouragement, Andrea seemed apathetic and showed little interest in the conversation. She reported a mild headache and asked for pain relief, which was administered as per her care plan. Andrea also needed full assistance with eating lunch but ate only a few spoonfuls before saying she felt nauseous again.

Betty spent most of the morning in her wheelchair. She seemed more disoriented today and repeatedly asked where she was. The reddened area on her left heel appeared more irritated despite regular repositioning. Betty needed help with brushing her teeth and dressing but was cooperative during these routines. Lunch was a challenge; she managed only a few sips of water and a small portion of pudding before refusing to eat more.

Carlos experienced severe back pain today, and his discomfort was visibly affecting his mood. He was reluctant to participate in the morning activities and preferred to lie down. Carlos was given IM pain relief, but it provided only temporary relief. During the night, he was restless and wandered out of his room twice. Efforts to calm and reorient him took longer than usual.

Dolores showed signs of increased agitation around midday. She complained of difficulty breathing, although her oxygen levels were stable. She was repositioned several times to ensure comfort, and her inhaler was administered. Dolores required assistance with toileting and dressing in the evening, and she was unable to finish her dinner despite encouragement and support. She mentioned feeling very tired but found it difficult to sleep.

Frank experienced a fall today while trying to transfer from his chair to the bed. No injuries were noted, but he appeared shaken and more confused afterwards. His nails were trimmed, as they had grown quite long, causing discomfort. Frank needed help eating and managed to take in some soup and water with support. He was observed frequently throughout the night due to concerns about his disorientation and potential for further falls.

Andrea showed signs of significant discomfort today. She experienced severe back pain which escalated after her afternoon nap. Despite being administered her scheduled pain relief, the pain persisted. We provided additional support with repositioning and use of heat packs. Awaiting follow-up with the palliative care team for further pain management strategies.

Elderly patient Ruth had a difficult time dressing today due to marked weakness in her limbs. She required full assistance with washing, dressing, and brushing her teeth in the morning. She also demonstrated little interest in social activities and chose to stay in her room, showing signs of apathy. Scheduled for a care plan discussion with the family to address her increasing care needs.

John vomited yesterday night and has been unable to keep any food down since breakfast today. An attempt to hydrate him frequently was made, but he is showing signs of dehydration. Clinician on duty decided to start subcutaneous fluids to maintain hydration. We documented his non-responsive state and have contacted the GP for an emergency review.

Emily has been struggling with persistent itching and swelling around her ankles, diagnosed as oedema. Her nails are also noticeably long and require trimming. Despite routine skin care, she has developed redness and peeling over the affected area. The palliative care nurse has been informed to adjust her skin care and evaluate her medications.

George has been extremely restless tonight, repeatedly trying to get up from bed and wander around his room. He appears confused and doesn't recognize his surroundings. Staff provided verbal comfort and physical reassurance without much success. Scheduled check-ins throughout the night to ensure his safety and awaiting psychologist follow-up for potential medication adjustment.

Andrea complained of severe back pain throughout the day. She received her regular dose of pain medication but reported minimal relief. Additional comfort measures were offered, including repositioning and the use of heat packs. She remains restless and is showing signs of increased discomfort. Awaiting evaluation by the palliative care team.

John did not sleep well last night, experiencing regular bouts of breathlessness. He required supplemental oxygen and several interventions to calm his anxiety. Despite many efforts, he was unable to find a comfortable position to alleviate his distress. Today, nursing staff will focus on reassessing his comfort needs and discussing with his family about potential changes to his care plan.

Maria's skin condition has rapidly worsened, with new pressure ulcers developing on her sacrum and heels. Regular repositioning and wound care have been provided without sufficiently preventing deterioration. Conversation with her GP has been initiated to review her current pain management and explore additional palliative options.

Betty has shown increased signs of agitation and confusion throughout the day. She repeatedly tried to get out of bed, resulting in two fall incidents, thankfully without injury. Nursing staff provided more one-on-one supervision and adjusted her environment to reduce potential risks. Discussion regarding the introduction of additional calming measures or medications has been scheduled with her healthcare provider.

Tom was noted to be more withdrawn and less interactive with fellow residents today. He did not engage in any organized activities and declined his meals and drinks. Nursing staff provided encouragement and support, offering small sips of water and easy-to-swallow snacks, but he remained disinterested. Continuous assessment of Tom's palliative care needs is ongoing and a family meeting is planned to reassess his current needs and care priorities.

Resident Sarah experienced significant back pain throughout the day, despite being given her prescribed analgesics. She required several position changes and additional comfort measures to find some relief. It was also noted that Sarah had no appetite during both lunch and dinner. Subcutaneous pain medication has been administered, and her physician has been contacted for further pain management guidance. Family has been informed and is considering increasing her palliative care support.

Zachary showed marked restlessness and agitation during the night, frequently getting up from bed and attempting to walk without his walker. This led to a minor fall in the early hours, though no injuries were sustained, just a mild fright. IM sedation was given as ordered, and ongoing one-to-one supervision has been arranged. He has also been more confused and disoriented than usual. A consult with the palliative care team is being scheduled to review his meds and overall plan.

Charlotte has had a difficult day, reporting tightness of breath and heightened discomfort, which hindered her participation in any of the daily activities. She has developed a pressure ulcer on her right hip, which has been assessed and dressed accordingly. Despite receiving oxygen therapy, she remains short of breath and anxious. The palliative care nurse has been notified to consider advanced comfort measures and potentially adjust her current treatment regimen.

Ethan spent a restless night, experiencing persistent nausea and vomiting that could not be controlled with anti-emetics. He declined breakfast and only managed a small portion of clear soup at lunch before vomiting again. He has been commenced on IV fluids due to decreased oral intake and signs of dehydration. Palliative care consultation is being sought to manage Ethan's symptoms more effectively and to provide additional support.

Madeline's edema has significantly worsened, extending to both lower extremities despite routine elevation and compressive stockings. She expressed discomfort and pain in the affected areas. Madeline was also noted to be deeply apathetic, engaging minimally with both staff and visitors. The palliative care team has been called in for an in-depth review to adjust her care plan to better address both her physical and emotional symptoms.

Mrs. Thompson exhibited signs of increased restlessness and agitation throughout the morning, displaying difficulty remaining seated and pacing her room. She mentioned experiencing sharp back pain, which was slightly alleviated with prescribed analgesics but persisted intermittently. A thorough review of her pain management plan is necessary. She refused lunch entirely, noting severe nausea, and has been commenced on subcutaneous fluids to maintain hydration.

Mr. Lopez has been non-verbal and disengaged with the usual morning activities. He displayed considerable difficulty with ambulation due to worsening oedema in his legs and required use of a wheelchair for transfers today. Despite encouragement, he only managed to eat a few spoonfuls of oatmeal at breakfast. A family member has requested a meeting to review and update his care plan, citing concerns about his declining physical health.

Ms. Patel experienced notable pressure ulcers on her heels and sacral area, requiring repositioning every two hours for relief. She has demonstrated significant confusion, unable to recognize familiar faces or understand her surroundings this afternoon. Hospice care has provided a new topical medication to address her peeling and itching skin, however, continued monitoring is needed for effectiveness.

Mr. Brown showed signs of increased breathlessness during his afternoon walk with a mobility aid. His oxygen saturation levels were monitored and found to be slightly below normal ranges. Despite experiencing severe nausea, he managed to consume half a bowl of soup for lunch but subsequently vomited. IM Zofran was administered with moderate relief. He reports tightness in his chest and further evaluation by the palliative care team is pending.

Ms. Nguyen has had difficulty communicating her needs and appeared apathetic during social hour, staring blankly at a magazine without turning the pages. She continues to suffer from chronic abdominal pain that has worsened, requiring a bolus of her PRN analgesic. She remains bedridden this evening due to general weakness and a lack of energy. Her overnight care will include frequent checks and repositioning assistance as necessary.
